mainTopic: Which payments to a זונה become forbidden for the מזבח, and whether the offspring and products of forbidden animals share their status
overview: The גמרא shows from the wording of the פסוק that relations with an animal are not זנות. A ברייתא adds that only אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב are forbidden, and not their offspring. רבא rules that the offspring of a pregnant נרבעת or נוגחת is forbidden, and there are two versions of his ruling on the offspring of a מוקצה or נעבד. רב teaches that קידושין with the dung of a שור הנסקל works, but not with the dung of עבודה זרה calves, and the גמרא gives a reason from logic and one from the פסוקים. A new משנה lists which payments to a זונה become forbidden: wine, oil, flour and birds do, while money and מוקדשין do not. It also teaches that the offspring of animals forbidden for the מזבח are permitted, with stricter views about a טרפה. The גמרא discusses a payment that changed form (a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל), what the words 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' teach, and why a פסוק was needed to exclude מוקדשין, answered with רבי's view on sharing a פסח. It ends with different versions of exactly where רבי אליעזר and the רבנן disagree about the offspring of a נרבעת.

steps.title: Where do we learn that there is no prostitution with animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that relations with an animal do not make a woman a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know what the Rabbis said, that there is no זנות with animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for a rule the חכמים stated: relations with an animal are not counted as זנות. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If relations with an animal counted as זנות, then payment for them would be a forbidden אתנן זונה. The משנה treated such payment as permitted, so the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Prostitution. Here it is the status that makes a payment into a forbidden אֶתְנַן.
Animals
From where is this matter? A request for a source.

phrases.english: From where is this matter
that the Rabbis said

phrases.notes: He means a woman who has relations with an animal is not called a זונה, so payment for it is not a forbidden אתנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a request for a source for a rule from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק shows that relations with an animal are not זנות.

steps.title: The verse could have written 'payment of a prostitute and a dog'
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from how the פסוק is worded: the Torah separates the dog case from the זונה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Nothing would have stopped the פסוק from writing 'the אתנן of a זונה and a dog'.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer points to the exact wording of the פסוק. The Torah could have joined the dog to 'אתנן זונה' but chose not to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק actually says 'אתנן זונה ומחיר כלב', which makes two separate categories. If the dog case were a kind of זנות, the Torah could simply have written 'אתנן זונה וכלב'. Since it did not, payment for relations with an animal is not זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A payment given for forbidden relations. An animal given as אֶתְנַן may not be brought on the מזבח.
Prostitute

phrases.notes: The real פסוק (דברים 23:19) says "אתנן זונה ומחיר כלב". Since it adds "מחיר", the dog case is not זנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording 'ומחיר כלב' rather than 'אתנן זונה וכלב' shows that the dog case is not counted as זנות.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: two and not four
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה are permitted, because the פסוק says 'שניהם', only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: From where do we know that the payment for a dog and the price of a זונה are permitted? Because the פסוק says 'two', and not four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with the answer it just gave. The ברייתא says the reversed cases are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'גם שניהם', meaning 'both of them', so only two things are forbidden: אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב. Switching the cases creates two more combinations, אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה. The word 'two' excludes them, so they are permitted on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Price. An animal received in exchange for something, here a dog, or a זונה bought as a maidservant.
Payment given for relations with a dog
Two and not four. Only the two cases the פסוק names are forbidden.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the pairs. אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב are FORBIDDEN. The reversed pair, אתנן כלב and מחיר זונה, is PERMITTED.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a baraita:

and the price of a prostitute are permitted?
As it says "two"

phrases.english: and not four.

steps.raayaObject: The rule that payment connected to a dog in the reversed way, and the price of a זונה, are not forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'שניהם' in דברים 23:19 as limiting the rule to two cases.

steps.title: The offspring of אתנן and מחיר are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the offspring of an animal given as אתנן or מחיר may be offered, because the פסוק says 'הם', only them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring are permitted, since it says 'גם שניהם'. 'Them' are forbidden, and not their offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds a second rule about the babies of these forbidden animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שניהם' contains 'הם', which means 'them'. That limits the prohibition to the animals actually given, so a baby born to them later is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring
Even both of them, words from the פסוק
Them and not others. A limiting reading of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Their offspring are permitted,
as it says "even both of them" —
"them" and not their offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a further rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring of an animal given as אתנן or מחיר may be brought as a קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question that רבא takes up next: what about the offspring of other animals that are forbidden for the מזבח?

steps.title: רבא: the offspring of a נרבעת or a נוגחת is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the baby of an animal that was used for bestiality, or that gored, is also forbidden, because the baby was part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The offspring of a נרבעת is forbidden, since she and her offspring were both used for bestiality. The offspring of a goring animal is forbidden, since she and her offspring both gored.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא turns to other animals that are forbidden for the מזבח and says their babies are forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases are different from אתנן. Here the act happened to the animal's body while it was pregnant, so the unborn baby counts as having taken part. That is why the baby carries the same status as its mother.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that a person used for bestiality. It is forbidden for the מזבח.
A goring animal, one that killed a person. It is forbidden for the מזבח.
Forbidden, here meaning forbidden as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: This is talking about an animal that was pregnant when the act happened. That is why the baby is treated as if it was involved too.

phrases.english: Rava said:

for she and her offspring were both used for bestiality.
The offspring of a goring animal is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The word "offspring" is not written here, but it carries over from the case just before.

phrases.english: for she and her offspring both gored.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the offspring of אתנן and מחיר to the offspring of other forbidden animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of a נרבעת or a נוגחת is forbidden for the מזבח, because the unborn baby took part in the act.

steps.title: The offspring of a מוקצה or a נעבד is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: the baby of an animal set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped, is permitted, since only the mother was involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of a מוקצה and of a נעבד is permitted. Why? It was the mother he set aside, and it was the mother they worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives the opposite ruling for two other forbidden animals and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idol worshipper's intent was aimed only at the mother animal. In this view the baby inside her was not included, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside to be used for idol worship
An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol
What is the reason?
He set it aside

phrases.english: The offspring of a set-aside animal or a worshipped animal is permitted.
What is the reason? It was its mother that he set aside,
it was its mother that they worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting ruling. Unlike נרבעת and נוגחת, the offspring here is permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of a מוקצה or a נעבד is permitted, because only the mother was the target of the worship.

steps.title: Another version: the offspring of a מוקצה or a נעבד is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבא's ruling the other way: the baby is forbidden, because the worshipper likes the animal's pregnant bulk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the offspring of a מוקצה and of a נעבד is forbidden. Why? Because he is pleased with its bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's ruling that reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the person who set aside or worshipped the animal liked its large pregnant size. That means the baby was part of what he valued, so it is included and forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is pleasing to him
Its bulk or swelling, meaning the size of the pregnant animal

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring of אתנן and מחיר: permitted. Offspring of נרבעת and נוגחת: forbidden, because the baby took part. Offspring of מוקצה and נעבד: depends on the version of רבא. It is permitted if only the mother was targeted, and forbidden if the worshipper valued her pregnant bulk.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
The offspring of a set-aside animal or a worshipped animal is forbidden.
What is the reason? Because he is pleased with its bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבא's ruling from step 6, with the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the offspring of a מוקצה or a נעבד is forbidden, because the worshipper valued the pregnant animal's size.

steps.title: Betrothing with the dung of a stoned ox versus idol-worship calves
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that קידושין done with the dung of a שור הנסקל works, but קידושין done with the dung of calves used for עבודה זרה does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי says in the name of רב: If a man betroths a woman with the dung of an ox that is going to be stoned, she is betrothed. If he uses the dung of calves that were used for idol worship, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב that compares two forbidden animals. It asks whether their dung is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not benefit from a שור הנסקל, and you may not benefit from an animal of עבודה זרה. רב says the dung of the stoned ox is permitted, so it has value and can be used for קידושין. The dung of the idol calves is forbidden, so it is worthless and the קידושין fails.

keyTerms.meaning: One who betroths a woman (does קִדּוּשִׁין by giving her something of value)
Dung, the waste inside or coming from an animal
An ox sentenced to be stoned (for example, because it killed a person). You may not benefit from it
Calves used for idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the dung being 'holy' or 'impure'. The only question is whether you may benefit from it. If you may not benefit from it, it has no value, and you cannot betroth a woman with it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַב:

One who betroths a woman with the dung of an ox that is to be stoned: she is betrothed.

phrases.english: With the dung of calves of idol worship, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of רבא's rulings about whether something that comes from a forbidden animal (its baby) shares the animal's status. Here the item is dung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dung of a שור הנסקל is permitted, so קידושין with it works. The dung of עבודה זרה calves is forbidden, so קידושין with it fails.

steps.title: What is the reason for the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two kinds of dung are treated differently. It says there are two possible answers: one from a פסוק and one from logic.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you want, say it comes from a verse. If you want, say it comes from logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling. It announces two ways to explain it, which sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals are forbidden for benefit, so why does the ban spread to the dung in only one case? The גמרא promises a logical reason and a reason from a פסוק. It then explains them one at a time, starting with the logic.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
If you wish, say… (introduces one of several possible explanations)
A verse (a reason taken from the תּוֹרָה)
Logical reasoning

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the dung of עבודה זרה calves forbidden, while the dung of a שור הנסקל is permitted?

steps.title: The logical reason: the idol worshipper wants the animal's bulk
steps.stepSummary: The idol worshipper is pleased that his calf looks big and full, dung included. So the dung is part of what he offers. Nobody gains anything from the bulk of a stoned ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say it is from logic: with idol worship, he is pleased with the animal's bulk. With a stoned ox, he gets nothing out of its bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation: a logical reason based on what the person actually cares about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol worshipper wants a big, impressive animal. The dung inside adds to its size, so it counts as part of the worship and is forbidden. A stoned ox is simply killed, and nobody cares how big it is, so the dung is not part of what is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It pleases him, he is happy with it
Its bulk or girth, how swollen and big it looks
Regarding, in the case of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same idea from step 7: the worshipper likes the animal's pregnant bulk, so the baby is forbidden. The idea of 'what the worshipper values counts as part of the worship' links the two rulings.

phrases.aramaic: נִיחָא לֵיהּ גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּנִיפְחֵיהּ,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The idol worshipper values the animal's bulk, so its dung is part of the worship. No one values a stoned ox's bulk.

steps.title: The reason from the verses: anything from an idol is like the idol, but only the ox's meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: For עבודה זרה the פסוק says 'והיית חרם כמוהו', which teaches that anything coming from it is like it. For the שור הנסקל the פסוק forbids only 'its meat', so its dung is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say it is from a verse. About idol worship it says 'and you will be banned like it': anything you get from it is like it. About the stoned ox it says 'its meat shall not be eaten': its meat is forbidden, its dung is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second explanation, which reads two פסוקים closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְהָיִיתָ' is read as if it said 'מְהַיֶּה', meaning to produce or bring into being. So whatever comes from the idol takes on its forbidden status. For the stoned ox the תורה names only 'בְּשָׂרוֹ' (its meat), which shows that other parts, like dung, are not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Something banned and forbidden
Produce, bring into being (a play on the word וְהָיִיתָ)
Like it, having the same status
Its meat

steps.whatToRemember: The dung of עבודה זרה is forbidden, and the dung of a שור הנסקל is permitted. There are two reasons: logic (the worshipper wants the bulk) and the פסוקים (anything 'produced' from an idol is like it, while the stoned ox has only 'its meat' forbidden).

steps.title: New משנה: which items given as a harlot's payment become forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Money given as אתנן may be used for the מזבח. Wine, oil, flour or anything else of a kind that is offered on the מזבח becomes forbidden. Items that were already מוקדשין stay permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he gave her money, it is permitted. Wines, oils, flours, and anything whose kind is offered on the altar, are forbidden. If he gave her consecrated items, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out which items given to a זונה as payment become forbidden to bring to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban of אתנן only takes effect on items of a kind that are actually offered on the מזבח. So coins, which are never offered themselves, stay permitted, while wine, oil and flour become forbidden. Things that were already מוקדשין stay permitted, because the giver does not own them and cannot make them forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A payment given to a זוֹנָה; the תורה forbids bringing it to the מִזְבֵּחַ
Money, coins
Fine flours (used for מְנָחוֹת)
Something of the same kind as it
Items already consecrated to the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted' with money does not mean paying a זונה is fine! It only means the coins themselves do not become forbidden for buying a קרבן.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money given as אתנן stays permitted. Things of a kind offered on the מזבח become forbidden. מוקדשין given as payment stay permitted.

steps.title: Birds given as payment are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that ordinary birds given as אתנן are forbidden for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds that were given as payment to a זונה are forbidden to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list from step 12 and gives a short ruling: birds given as אתנן are forbidden. Right after this it explains why a special source is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 taught that items that were already מוקדשין stay permitted even if given as אתנן. Now the משנה says ordinary birds are different and do become forbidden. This sets up the next lines, which explain why we might have thought otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds (here, ordinary birds that were not yet sanctified)
Payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought to the מקדש

phrases.english: Birds — these are forbidden,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of what becomes forbidden as אתנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary birds given as אתנן are forbidden for the מזבח.

steps.title: Logic would have permitted birds
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a קל וחומר suggesting that birds should NOT become forbidden as אתנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Logic would say this: sanctified animals can be disqualified by a blemish, and still the אתנן and מחיר prohibition does not take hold of them. A bird is not disqualified by a blemish. Surely, then, the אתנן and מחיר prohibition should not take hold of a bird either?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה builds a logical argument that points the opposite way from its ruling. It wants to show why a פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish disqualifies sanctified animals, which makes them 'stricter'. Yet the אתנן prohibition does not apply to them. Birds are 'more lenient' because a blemish does not disqualify them, so it seems the prohibition should not apply to birds either. This קל וחומר challenges the ruling of step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a stricter case to a more lenient case, or the reverse
A physical blemish that can disqualify an animal from being offered
The price received for a dog, which is also forbidden for the מקדש
Items already sanctified to the מקדש

phrases.english: If sanctified animals, which a blemish disqualifies —

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sanctified animals are stricter, because a blemish disqualifies them, and yet they are not affected by אתנן. So birds, which are more lenient, should not be affected either.

steps.title: The פסוק 'for any vow' includes birds
steps.stepSummary: The words 'לכל נדר' in the פסוק include birds in the אתנן prohibition, against the logic of the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says 'for any vow': it comes to include the bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the logical argument by pointing to an extra phrase in the פסוק that includes birds in the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone would have permitted birds. The phrase 'לכל נדר' ('for any vow') widens the prohibition, so it covers birds as well. The פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches', which introduces a source from the תורה
A vow
To include

steps.whatToRemember: Birds are forbidden as אתנן only because the פסוק 'לכל נדר' includes them. Logic by itself would have permitted them.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: 'For any vow' —
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19

phrases.english: to include the bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the קל וחומר of step 14 using a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds would be permitted because of the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Birds are forbidden because 'לכל נדר' includes them.

steps.title: Offspring of forbidden animals are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states a general rule: animals forbidden for the מזבח can still have offspring that are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: All animals that are forbidden for the מזבח: their offspring are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a broad rule: even if an animal is forbidden for the מזבח, its offspring may be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition rests on the animal itself and does not pass to its young. This rule covers animals like an אתנן or a מחיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring
With regard to the מזבח, meaning to be offered on it

phrases.english: All those forbidden for the altar —
their offspring are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New rule in the משנה, about offspring
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring of animals forbidden for the מזבח are permitted.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: offspring of a טרפה is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that the offspring of a טרפה may not be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the offspring of a טרפה may not be offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the general rule in one case: the young of a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 16 permits offspring. רבי אליעזר makes an exception when the mother is a טרפה, and he forbids the offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal wound or defect, which is forbidden to eat
The offspring of

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: וְלַד טְרֵפָה לֹא יִקְרַב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: The offspring of a tereifa shall not be offered on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 16 in the case of a טרפה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of a טרפה is forbidden for the מזבח.

steps.title: An animal that nursed from a טרפה is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס goes further and disqualifies a healthy animal that nursed from a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: a healthy animal that nursed from a טרפה is disqualified from the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion in the משנה, stricter still: even nursing from a טרפה disqualifies an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר spoke only about an offspring. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס disqualifies even an unrelated healthy animal that drank the milk of a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A healthy, valid animal
Nursed, drank milk
Disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
A valid animal that nursed from a tereifa —
is disqualified from the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further strict view about a טרפה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valid animal that nursed from a טרפה is disqualified from the מזבח.

steps.title: קדשים that became טרפה are not redeemed
steps.stepSummary: Sanctified animals that became טרפה may not be redeemed, because we do not redeem קדשים just to feed them to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: All sanctified animals that became טרפה may not be redeemed, because we do not redeem קדשים in order to feed them to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a rule about sanctified animals that became טרפה: they may not be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redemption usually lets a person use a disqualified sanctified animal. A טרפה cannot be eaten, though, so after redemption its only use would be dog food. That would be disrespectful to קדשים, so redemption is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeem, making the animal non-sacred by paying its value
Sanctified animals
Dogs

steps.whatToRemember: We do not redeem a sanctified טרפה, because the only use left for it would be feeding dogs.

phrases.english: All sanctified animals that became tereifa —
one may not redeem them,
for one does not redeem sanctified animals
to feed them to dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final rule in the משנה, still on the topic of טרפה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sanctified animals that became טרפה may not be redeemed.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about a changed payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that disagree about whether wheat, olives or grapes that were turned into flour, oil or wine stay forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: if he gave her wheat and she made it into flour, olives and she made them into oil, or grapes and she made them into wine, one ברייתא says they are forbidden and another says they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a new question: does an אתנן stay forbidden after it changes form? It sets two sources against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says the new product is still forbidden. The other says the change makes it permitted. This contradiction needs a resolution, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
If he gave her wheat and she made it into flour,
olives and she made them into oil,
grapes and she made them into wine.
One baraita teaches: they are forbidden,
and another baraita teaches: they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: אֲסוּרִים, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a case of a changed אתנן
steps.kashyaTarget: The status of an אתנן that changed form
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on the same case.

steps.title: It is a מחלוקת of בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites a ברייתא from גוריון of אספורק showing that the two ברייתות reflect a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: גוריון of אספורק teaches that בית שמאי forbid them and בית הלל permit them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction. The two ברייתות are not really fighting; each one follows a different school.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that forbids follows בית שמאי, and the one that permits follows בית הלל. The contradiction becomes a known מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbid
Permit

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Guryon of Aspork teaches —
Beit Shammai forbid
and Beit Hillel permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תָּנֵי גּוּרְיוֹן דְּמִן אַסְפּוֹרַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion (בית שמאי and בית הלל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidding ברייתא follows בית שמאי and the permitting one follows בית הלל.

steps.title: בית הלל's source: 'הם' excludes offspring and changes
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל read the word 'הם' in the פסוק as limiting the prohibition to the original items, not their offspring and not their changed form.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל hold: 'them' and not their offspring; 'them' and not their changed forms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where בית הלל learn their lenient view. They learn it from the word 'הם' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הם' limits the prohibition to the very items given. One 'הם' excludes offspring, which matches step 16. A second 'הם' excludes items that changed form, so flour made from wheat is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, or they reason
A change in the item's form

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית הלל, the word 'הם' limits the אתנן prohibition to the original item. Its offspring and its changed forms are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's rule that offspring are permitted, and it gives the source for ruling that a changed item is no longer the forbidden אתנן.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel hold:
'Them' — and not their offspring,
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19, which says 'גם שניהם', 'even both of them'.

phrases.english: 'Them' — and not their changed forms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for בית הלל's lenient view in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on 'הם', the prohibition applies only to the original items, not to their offspring and not to their changed forms.

steps.title: How בית שמאי read the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי agree that 'הם' excludes offspring, but they read 'גם' as including the items after they have changed form.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold: 'Them' means not their offspring. 'Even' comes to include them after they have changed.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we heard בית הלל's reading, the גמרא shows how בית שמאי read the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the word 'הם' excludes offspring. The difference is that בית שמאי also use the word 'גם' ('even') to add something back in. For them, wheat that became flour, or grapes that became wine, stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring (babies of the animals given as payment)
To include; the word adds a case to the rule
Their changed forms (flour from wheat, oil from olives, wine from grapes)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
"Them" — but not their offspring,
"Even" — to include their changed forms.
phrases.notes: Both words come from the same פסוק: "כי תועבת ה׳ אלהיך גם שניהם" (דברים 23:19).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute that was explained in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, changed forms of an אתנן stay forbidden ('גם'), but offspring are permitted ('הם').

steps.title: What does בית הלל do with the word 'גם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בית הלל explain the word 'גם' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בית הלל, isn't it written 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: the word 'גם' is right there in the פסוק, so what do they learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in a פסוק should teach something. בית שמאי use 'גם' to include changed forms. בית הלל permit changed forms, so the word seems to have no job in their reading.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written...? (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: And according to Beit Hillel — isn't it written "even"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בית הלל in light of בית שמאי's use of 'גם' in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's reading of the פסוק (Step 22)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'גם' must teach something. If בית הלל permit changed forms, the word is left without a purpose.

steps.title: The word 'גם' stays difficult for בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer: 'גם' remains a difficulty for בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Even' is difficult for בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer the question. It simply admits that the word 'גם' is a problem for בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קשיא' here means the question stands without an answer. This does not disprove בית הלל's view; it only leaves one word in the פסוק unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty; here, a question that is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: changed forms and offspring of an אתנן are permitted ('הם'). בית שמאי: offspring are permitted, but changed forms are forbidden ('גם'). The word 'גם' remains unexplained for בית הלל.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not the same as 'תיובתא'. A קשיא leaves a question open; it does not reject the opinion.

phrases.english: "Even" is difficult according to Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of Step 24 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question on בית הלל from the word 'גם' is left unanswered.

steps.title: What 'the House of ה׳ your God' excludes and includes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אלעזר says the words 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' exclude the פרה אדומה, while חכמים say they include gold plates.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'The House of ה׳ your God' excludes the red heifer, since it is not brought into the House. These are the words of רבי אלעזר. The חכמים say it comes to include beaten gold plates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא that argues about what the words 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' in the פסוק of אתנן teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the words as a limit: the ban only applies to something that comes into the בית המקדש. So a פרה אדומה bought with an אתנן is allowed, since it is done outside. חכמים read the words as an addition: even gold plates used to decorate the בית המקדש may not come from an אתנן.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; this case is left out of the rule
The red heifer, which was burned outside the בית המקדש
Thin, beaten plates of gold used to cover parts of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"The House of the Lord your God" —
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19. The פסוק says not to bring an אתנן or a מחיר כלב into the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: excludes a red heifer,
since it is not brought into the House;
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar.
And the Sages say:
It comes to include the beaten plates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the same פסוק of אתנן, now looking at the words 'בית ה׳ אלהיך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: a פרה אדומה is not covered by the ban. חכמים: gold plates for the בית המקדש are covered by the ban.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which sage holds the view of the חכמים in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which specific sage holds the view of the unnamed 'חכמים' who include gold plates. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the view without a name. The גמרא wants to connect it to a known sage who holds this idea elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Who? (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the identity of the חכמים in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name of the sage who holds that gold plates are included in the ban.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the חכמים are רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who rules that gold paid to a זונה may not be made into plates even for the area behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. As it was taught: If he gave her gold, רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: One may not make beaten plates from it, even for behind the בית הכפורת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question and brings a ברייתא to show that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second ברייתא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה forbids using an אתנן of gold for plates in the בית המקדש. He says this applies even to the area behind the קודש הקדשים, which is less holy. This matches the חכמים who 'include the plates'.

keyTerms.meaning: The room of the כפורת (the ark cover), meaning the קודש הקדשים
Behind; the space at the back of the building

steps.whatToRemember: The 'חכמים' who include gold plates in the ban are רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. In his view, even plates for a less holy area may not come from an אתנן.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught: If he gave her gold,
Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
One may not make beaten plates from it,
even for behind the Hall of the Ark Cover.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, as shown by his ruling that gold from an אתנן may not be made into plates even for behind the בית הכפורת.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: paying a זונה with consecrated items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if he paid her with מוקדשין, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave her consecrated items, they are permitted, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next case. This line sets up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that consecrated items given to a זונה are not forbidden as an אתנן. The reason is simple: they do not belong to him, so they cannot become her payment. The word 'כו׳' tells us the משנה continues, and that the rest of the line will be discussed next.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated items (already set aside for the בית המקדש)
Permitted
'Etc.'; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: If he gave her consecrated items —
they are permitted, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: birds that are not consecrated, given as payment, are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן לָהּ מוּקְדָּשִׁין הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא about 'בית ה׳ אלהיך' and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated items given to a זונה as payment are permitted for the מזבח.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: consecrated animals should become אתנן too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אתנן and מחיר should apply to מוקדשין, using a קל וחומר from birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the rules of אתנן and מחיר apply to consecrated animals, by a קל וחומר. Birds are not disqualified by a blemish, and still אתנן and מחיר apply to them. Consecrated animals are disqualified by a blemish, so surely אתנן and מחיר should apply to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that consecrated animals given as payment stay permitted. It argues they should become forbidden. This sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds are less strict than animals, because a blemish does not disqualify a bird as a קרבן. Yet birds can still become forbidden as אתנן. Consecrated animals are stricter, since a blemish does disqualify them, so it would seem logical that they can become forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated items, animals already set aside for the בית המקדש
Payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought as a קרבן
The price of a dog, meaning an animal traded for a dog, which may not be brought as a קרבן
A logical argument: if the easier case has this rule, the stricter case surely does
A physical blemish that disqualifies an animal as a קרבן

phrases.english: But let consecrated animals
have the rules of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog apply to them,
by an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עוֹפוֹת שֶׁאֵין הַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן —
phrases.english: If birds, which a blemish does not disqualify,
still have payment and price apply to them,
then consecrated animals, which a blemish does disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן?
phrases.english: is it not logical that payment and price should apply to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִהְיוּ מוּקְדָּשִׁין אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling, quoted in step 29, that מוקדשין given as payment are permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that consecrated animals given to a זונה remain permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from birds: if the easier case, birds, becomes forbidden, the stricter case, consecrated animals, should too.

steps.title: The פסוק 'לכל נדר' leaves out consecrated animals
steps.stepSummary: The word נדר in the פסוק excludes animals that were already vowed, so the קל וחומר does not hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'for any vow.' This comes to leave out what was already vowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own קל וחומר with a פסוק. The פסוק shows that consecrated animals do not become אתנן or מחיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is written about bringing these things 'for any vow.' The גמרא reads this as speaking only about items that are not yet vowed. An animal that is already consecrated is therefore excluded, whatever the logic of the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us
To exclude, to leave out
Something already vowed or consecrated

steps.whatToRemember: Consecrated animals given to a זונה are not forbidden as אתנן. A פסוק, 'לכל נדר', excludes them, even though logic alone might have said otherwise.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: “For any vow,”
phrases.notes: דברים 23:19

phrases.english: to exclude what has already been vowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 30 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural exclusion that overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר from birds would make consecrated animals forbidden as אתנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word נדר excludes items already vowed, so consecrated animals stay permitted.

steps.title: Why was a פסוק needed, if consecrated animals are not his?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק was needed, since a person cannot make forbidden something that does not belong to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason they are permitted is that the פסוק excluded them. Had the פסוק not excluded them, would I have said that if he gives her consecrated animals, אתנן and מחיר apply? But they are not his property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges this derivation. Why would anyone think consecrated animals could become אתנן in the first place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A consecrated animal belongs to הקדש, not to the person. A person cannot make forbidden something that is not his. So consecrated animals should be permitted even without a פסוק, and the גמרא wants to know what case this derivation is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
The פסוק excluded them
I would have thought (the initial assumption)
His own money or property

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying consecrated animals become אתנן. It is asking why a פסוק was needed at all, since they are not his to make forbidden.

phrases.english: The reason is that the verse excluded them;
but had the verse not excluded them,
I would have said:
when he gives her consecrated animals,
payment and price apply to them?
But it is not his property!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּמַעֲטִינְהוּ קְרָא, הָא לָא מַעֲטִינְהוּ קְרָא הֲוָה אֲמִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the exclusion in step 31 was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a פסוק to exclude מוקדשין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrated animals are not the giver's property, so they could never become forbidden as אתנן, even without a פסוק.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: he registered her on his קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא says the case is someone who pays the זונה by registering her for a share in his קרבן פסח, following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: the case is one who registers her for a share of his פסח. This follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא explains when a consecrated animal could count as his. The case is a share in his קרבן פסח given as payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a person has a kind of ownership in his פסח, since he may sell shares in it to others for money. Because of this, giving the זונה a share in it could count as giving her something of value that is his. That is why a פסוק was needed to exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: Registers someone as a participant in a קרבן
The קרבן פסח, the Paschal lamb

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that a consecrated animal can sometimes have a money value to its owner. That is why the פסוק's exclusion is needed.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya says:
It is referring to one who registers her for his Paschal offering,
phrases.notes: He pays her by giving her a share in his פסח.

phrases.english: and it follows the view of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: בְּמַמְנֶה עַל פִּסְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 32 by pointing to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Consecrated animals are never his property, so no פסוק should be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי, a share in one's פסח has money value to him, so a פסוק is needed to exclude it.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: the first opinion allows money from the פסח only for food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'מהיות משה' as 'sustain him from the lamb': he may get money from his פסח for food, but not for buying other things.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: 'And if the household is too small for a lamb.' Sustain him from the lamb. This is when he lacks enough to eat, but not when he lacks enough to buy other things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that רב הושעיא relies on. This step gives its first, anonymous opinion: a poor person may take money for shares in his פסח, but only to buy food. רבי's broader view follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מהיות משה' are read as 'החייהו משה', meaning keep him alive from the lamb. In the first opinion, a poor person may register others on his פסח for money, but only when he lacks food. רבי, in the next step, widens this, and רב הושעיא's case follows רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Sustain him from the lamb
From lacking enough to eat
A purchase, buying other things

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion in the ברייתא lets a poor person take money for shares in his פסח only to buy food. רבי, in the next step, allows it even for other purchases, and רב הושעיא's answer follows רבי.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
“And if the household be too little for a lamb.”
phrases.notes: שמות 12:4

phrases.english: Sustain him from the lamb,
phrases.notes: A play on the word מהיות, read like 'keep him alive': he may live off money from shares in the lamb.

phrases.english: when he lacks enough to eat, but not when he lacks enough to buy other things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי's view that step 33 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: The background to רבי's view: the first opinion's limited permission to take money for shares in one's פסח, which רבי then widens.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'מהיות משה' (שמות 12:4) as 'החייהו משה'.

steps.title: רבי allows registering others on his פסח even for non-food money
steps.stepSummary: רבי says a person may sign others onto his פסח and חגיגה even to get money for other purchases. The money is חולין because the Jewish people consecrate their פסח offerings on that condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Even if he needs money to buy other things, he may register others with him on his פסח and his חגיגה, and the money he gets is חולין. This is because the Jewish people consecrate their פסח offerings on exactly this condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step finishes with רבי's opinion. He is more lenient than the first opinion: you may take money for your פסח even for things other than food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allowed taking money from one's פסח only for food. רבי allows it for any need, because the הקדש was made on the condition that others could be added for money. This is the piece that backs up רב הושעיא in step 33: paying a זונה by registering her on one's פסח is a real case only according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Registers or signs someone up as a partner in a קרבן
The festival peace offering brought on יום טוב
Not holy, ordinary money that may be used freely
On this condition

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, money a person gets from registering others on his פסח is ordinary money and may be used for anything. That is why רב הושעיא could set the אתנן case according to רבי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the explanation of why the פסוק of אתנן was needed for מוקדשין. Because of רבי's condition, the פסח partly belongs to the owner, so without the פסוק 'לכל נדר' giving a share of it as payment could have made it forbidden as an אתנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: even to have enough to buy things
for if he does not have enough money
he may register others with him
on his Paschal offering and on his Festival offering
and his money is not holy
for it is on this condition
that the Jewish people consecrated their Paschal offerings

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 34 with רבי's broader opinion.
steps.raayaObject: רב הושעיא's claim that a person can pay a זונה by registering her on his פסח, according to רבי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'מהיות משה', which ends with רבי's opinion

steps.title: רב says רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring of altar-forbidden animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the offspring of animals forbidden for the מזבח are permitted. רב says a ברייתא adds that רבי אליעזר forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'All animals that are forbidden for the altar...' רב says: All animals that are forbidden for the altar, their offspring are permitted. And a ברייתא teaches about this: And רבי אליעזר forbids them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. רב points out that this rule is not agreed by everyone, because רבי אליעזר disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rule that the offspring are permitted belongs to the רבנן. רבי אליעזר holds that the offspring are forbidden like their mothers. This sets up the next two steps, which ask which exact case the dispute is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals forbidden to be brought on the altar
Their offspring
Forbids

phrases.english: All that are forbidden for the altar, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting our משנה, whose general rule covers animals like those used for bestiality (listed in an earlier משנה).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כָּל הָאֲסוּרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: Rav says: All that are forbidden for the altar
their offspring are permitted
and a ברייתא teaches about it: And Rabbi Eliezer forbids them

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הָאֲסוּרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אתנן discussion and moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of altar-forbidden animals are permitted according to the רבנן. רבי אליעזר forbids them.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the dispute is when pregnancy came before the bestiality
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the dispute is about an animal that became pregnant and only then was used for bestiality. רבי אליעזר holds that a fetus is part of its mother. If the bestiality came first, everyone agrees the offspring is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא says that רב נחמן says: The dispute is where the animals became pregnant and afterwards were used for bestiality. רבי אליעזר holds that a fetus is like its mother's thigh, and the רבנן hold that it is not like its mother's thigh. But if they were used for bestiality first and became pregnant afterwards, everyone agrees the offspring are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains the exact case of the dispute and the reason behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fetus was already inside when the mother became forbidden, the question is whether it counts as part of her body. רבי אליעזר says yes (עובר ירך אמו), so it becomes forbidden with her. The רבנן say no, so it stays permitted. If the pregnancy began only after the bestiality, the fetus was never part of the forbidden act, so everyone permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: They became pregnant
They were used for bestiality, which makes an animal forbidden for the מזבח
A fetus is like its mother's thigh, meaning it counts as part of the mother's body
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order of events. רב נחמן's dispute is pregnancy first, then bestiality. In the opposite order, he says everyone permits the offspring.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana says that Rav Nachman says:
The dispute is where they became pregnant
and afterwards were used for bestiality
for Rabbi Eliezer holds
'a fetus is its mother's thigh'
phrases.notes: The unborn calf counts as a body part of the mother, so it shares her status.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold
'it is not its mother's thigh'
but if they were used for bestiality and afterwards became pregnant
everyone agrees they are permitted

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the exact case of the dispute that רב reported.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only where pregnancy came before the bestiality, and it depends on whether עובר ירך אמו. If the bestiality came first, everyone permits the offspring.

steps.title: רבא: the dispute is when the bestiality came before the pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the dispute is about an animal used for bestiality that became pregnant afterwards. The question is the rule of זה וזה גורם: רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring and the רבנן permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: The dispute is where they were used for bestiality and afterwards became pregnant. רבי אליעזר holds that when this and that both cause something, it is forbidden, and the Rabbis hold that when this and that both cause something, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רב נחמן about which case the dispute covers. He places it in the opposite order of events and gives a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the offspring comes from two causes: a forbidden mother and a permitted father. רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם אסור, so the forbidden mother makes the offspring forbidden. The רבנן hold זה וזה גורם מותר, so the offspring is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: When two factors together cause something, here a forbidden mother and a permitted father
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן places the dispute at pregnancy before bestiality, based on עובר ירך אמו. רבא places it at bestiality before pregnancy, based on זה וזה גורם.

phrases.english: Rava says: The dispute is where they were used for bestiality
and afterwards became pregnant
for Rabbi Eliezer holds:
when this and that both cause something, it is forbidden
phrases.notes: 'This and that' are the forbidden mother and the permitted father, which together produce the offspring.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
when this and that both cause something, it is permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁנִּרְבְּעוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף עִיבְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from רב נחמן's of which case the dispute is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is where the bestiality came before the pregnancy, and it depends on זה וזה גורם. רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring and the רבנן permit it.

steps.title: רבא: pregnant first, bestiality after, everyone forbids
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his explanation. If the animal became pregnant first and was used for bestiality afterwards, everyone agrees the offspring is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the animals became pregnant and only afterwards were used for bestiality, everyone agrees they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation from the previous step. He tells us which case everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא placed the dispute in the case where the bestiality came first and the pregnancy came later; that case depends on זה וזה גורם. If the fetus was already inside the mother during the bestiality, it was involved in the act itself, so everyone forbids it. This is the opposite of רב נחמן, who said this exact case is the one under dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: They became pregnant
And afterwards
They were used for bestiality
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sages. רב נחמן says the dispute is when the pregnancy came first. רבא says that in this case everyone forbids, and the dispute is only when the bestiality came first.

phrases.english: But if they became pregnant and afterwards were used for bestiality,
everyone agrees they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל עיברו ולבסוף נרבעו דברי הכל אסורין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's statement from step 38 by naming the case where everyone agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the pregnancy came before the bestiality, the offspring is forbidden according to everyone.

steps.title: רבא is consistent with his own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's view fits another rule he taught. The offspring of a pregnant animal that was used for bestiality, or that gored, is forbidden, because the mother and the fetus both took part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: the offspring of an animal used for bestiality is forbidden, because she and her offspring were both used for bestiality. The offspring of a goring animal is forbidden, because she and her offspring both gored.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up step 39 by quoting another rule of רבא's that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a fetus inside its mother is treated as taking part in whatever is done to her or by her. So when a pregnant animal is used for bestiality, the fetus counts as used too. When a pregnant animal gores, the fetus counts as goring too. This is exactly why רבא said in step 39 that everyone forbids the offspring when the pregnancy came first.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his other rulings
Offspring
A goring animal

phrases.english: And רבא follows his own reasoning,
as רבא said:
the offspring of an animal used for bestiality is forbidden,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a mother that was already pregnant at the time.

phrases.english: since she and her offspring were both used for bestiality;
the offspring of a goring animal is forbidden,
since she and her offspring both gored.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 39 by showing that רבא holds the same idea elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that everyone forbids the offspring when the pregnancy came before the bestiality.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Another statement of רבא: a fetus counts as taking part in the bestiality or goring of its mother.

steps.title: Another version: the dispute is when the animal was already consecrated
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב הונא בר חיננא quotes רב נחמן. He says the dispute is about an animal used for bestiality while it was already מוקדש. רבי אליעזר treats this as a disgrace to the holy offering, and the רבנן do not. If the bestiality happened while the animal was still חולין, everyone permits the offspring, because the animal has since changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it in another version: רב הונא בר חיננא said that רב נחמן said: the dispute is where they were used for bestiality while they were consecrated. רבי אליעזר holds that it is a disgrace, and the רבנן hold that it is not. But if they were used for bestiality while they were non-sacred, since they have changed, everyone agrees they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a different version of the whole discussion. This time the question is whether the animal was holy or ordinary when the bestiality happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version no longer asks about pregnancy timing. It asks whether the act was done to a holy animal. רבי אליעזר says offering the offspring would be a disgrace, so it is forbidden; the רבנן disagree. If the act happened while the animal was still חולין, its status changed when it was consecrated afterwards, so everyone permits.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Consecrated; set aside as offerings
Ordinary, not holy
A disgrace counts; it is a real concern
Since they have changed status

phrases.english: Some say it in another version.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: רב הונא בר חיננא said that רב נחמן said:
The dispute is where they were used for bestiality while they were consecrated,
for רבי אליעזר holds that the disgrace is significant,
and the רבנן hold that it is not.
But if they were used for bestiality while they were non-sacred,
since they have changed,
phrases.notes: They went from ordinary to holy when they were consecrated afterwards.

phrases.english: everyone agrees they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לישנא אחרינא אמרי לה אמר רב הונא בר חיננא אמר רב נחמן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier version (steps 37 to 40) with a new way of defining the dispute: holy or ordinary at the time of the act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about bestiality done while the animal was מוקדש. If it was done while the animal was חולין, everyone permits.

steps.title: רבא's version of רב נחמן: the dispute is when the animal was ordinary
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן the opposite way. The dispute is about bestiality done while the animal was חולין. רבי אליעזר still treats it as a disgrace, while the רבנן permit because the animal has changed. If the bestiality happened while the animal was מוקדש, everyone forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that רב נחמן said: the dispute is where they were used for bestiality while they were non-sacred. רבי אליעזר holds that the disgrace is significant. The רבנן hold that since they have changed, they are permitted. But if they were used for bestiality while they were consecrated, everyone agrees they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different report of what רב נחמן said. It flips which case is disputed and which case everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the change from חולין to holy is the רבנן's reason for permitting. רבי אליעזר says the disgrace still matters even after the change. When the act was done to an animal that was already holy, there was no change at all, so even the רבנן forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: Dispute
Permitted
Forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reports of רב נחמן. Report 1 (רב הונא בר חיננא): the dispute is when the animal was holy, and if it was ordinary everyone permits. Report 2 (רבא): the dispute is when the animal was ordinary, and if it was holy everyone forbids.

phrases.english: רבא said that רב נחמן said:
The dispute is where they were used for bestiality while they were non-sacred,
for רבי אליעזר holds that the disgrace is significant,
and the רבנן hold that since they have changed, they are permitted,
but if they were used for bestiality while they were consecrated,
everyone agrees they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר רב נחמן מחלוקת כשנרבעו כשהן חולין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second report of רב נחמן that reverses the version in step 41.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about bestiality done while the animal was חולין. If it was done while the animal was מוקדש, everyone forbids.
steps.whyThisMatters: Comparing the two reports shows that the debate turns on one question: does an animal's change in status from ordinary to holy remove the disgrace of what was done to it?
